consensus_summary: All four blind responses converge on the highway as the divinely prepared way of the Lord, centered on Isaiah 35:8's 'Highway of Holiness' — the sanctified route by which the redeemed return to Zion/God — and Isaiah 40:3's prepared way for God's coming, applied in the Gospels to John the Baptist. Secondary strands (return from exile, Gentile inclusion, personal sanctification, repentance) are treated as complementary layers of this single motif.
book_summary: The book defines the highway as 'The way of holiness — the prepared road home,' citing Isaiah 35:8, i.e., the sanctified, God-prepared route by which the redeemed travel back to God.
consensus_core_identification: The highway is God's prepared way of holiness/salvation — the route by which He comes to His people and by which the redeemed return to Him (Isa 35:8; 40:3).
book_core_identification: The highway is the way of holiness, the prepared road by which the redeemed return home to God (Isa 35:8).
boundary_disagreement: None of substance. The book's gloss compresses the motif to the Isaiah 35:8 'holiness + return home' strand and does not explicitly mention the Isaiah 40:3/John-the-Baptist 'preparation for the Lord's coming' application, but this is a matter of brevity and emphasis, not exclusion — 'the prepared road home' directly restates the consensus's dominant reading of the redeemed returning to Zion.
material_contradiction: None. The book's identification is a near-verbatim restatement of the consensus primary meaning.
rationale: Every consensus response makes Isaiah 35:8's Way of Holiness the anchor of the primary meaning, described as the prepared route of the redeemed returning to Zion/God. The book's entry — 'The way of holiness — the prepared road home' with Isa 35:8 as its proof text — is that identification in condensed form. The elements 'holiness,' 'prepared,' and 'road home' map one-to-one onto the consensus components (Way of Holiness, prepared way, return of the redeemed). Differences (the book omits the Christological Isa 40:3 layer and alternative uses) are omissions of detail in a glossary line, not boundary changes or reclassifications, so REFINED is not warranted.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book narrows the symbol by dropping the Isaiah 40:3 'prepare the way for the Lord's coming' dimension (God coming to us, rather than us going home), which most responses treat as co-primary; a strict reader might call that a REFINED narrowing of the motif's direction. However, a one-line glossary gloss selecting the dominant Isa 35:8 strand does not deny or exclude the other strands, so MATCH remains the better classification.
